content:
Hello, I hope you have a great lunch with sweet potatoes and steamed fish.

Is anybody here on Lean working on "prismatic stable homotoy theory" as conjectured by Lurie in his ICM 2026 talk?

van Doorn had a Lean 2/hott formalization of spectra, generalized cohomology and AHSS spectral sequences; but are there recent progress in these areas?

Also Brunerie did compute pi_4(S^3) in Agda/hott by avoiding spectral sequences (but directly using its consequence, the Gysin sequence), and was that the main motivation or was that easier than going through homotopy-fiber F in ΩK(Z,3) -> F -> S^3 -> K(Z,3) but computing the more-connected F via SSS?

And would a "traditional proof assistant" such as Lean be able to do the same kind of algorithmic-computations (Grobner bases, etc) as a computer algebra system such as Singular?

And are such kind of algorithmic-computations, rather than only logic/proof computations, actually required by big VIP theorems such as Anthropic's FLT? i.e. anthropics/fermats-last-theorem mentions BoundedSpectralSequence but are actual algorithmic/CAS-computations used during the proof? and vs @Kevin Buzzard's FLT?

Overall is it a good idea to form a Caltech Mathathon team and throw OpenAI free tokens at Lurie's "prismatic conjecture", lol

How familiar are you with the kinds of machinery that Lurie assumes? That is, have you looked at Lurie's home page and the thousands of pages of dense technicalities? And that's not any of the prismatic stuff.
